workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§7–23
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§7–23: Alan-Qo'a and the Five Arrows
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§7–23, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Dobun-Mergen takes Alan-Qo'a to wife and dies; she bears three more sons without a husband, and teaches all five the lesson of the bundled arrows. Read for the grammar of the converb chain and the participle clause, for the reflexive-possessive endings (-beġen, -jüġen, -ben), and for ügei bolu- 'become without' (to die). Genealogy and household law share the stage: who is kin, who is given a share, and who is left out. Where I could not construe a form with confidence the note says so.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.l: Truly beautiful, good, fame and name great-having, Alan-Γoγ̇a name-having, to a man even not yet given, a girl there was.
sentences.i: there was a girl named Alan-Qo'a, truly beautiful and of great fame and name, who had not yet been given to any man.
sentences.n: Read the first twelve words as one long description that waits for its noun, ökin 'girl', at the very end. -tei is the possessive 'having' (jeketei 'great-having', neretei 'name-having' = named); it turns -tu / -tü / -tai by vowel harmony, and you will keep meeting it. ögteġei üdüġüi, Ming 與 未的 'not yet given': I take ögte- as a passive of ög- 'give' (compare ögdegsen in §8) and -ġei as the past ending of the pilot's ažiγ̇ai 'there was', so 'was given'; both are inferences, since the Ming glosses the whole word with the single character 與. ber after küġün-(n)e is 'even': 'to any man at all'.

sentences.l: Those, a division of people also: Köl-Barγužin Tögüm's master Barγudai-Mergen's daughter, Barγužin-Γoγ̇a name-having,
sentences.i: Those, too, were a band of people. Barqudai-Mergen was lord of Tögüm in Köl-Barqujin, and he had a daughter named Barqujin-Qo'a;
sentences.n: This is the first half of one sentence; the verb comes in the next unit. Every possessor stands before what it owns (Barγudai-Mergen-(n)ü ökin 'Barqudai's daughter'), so read the chain from the last link back. böleg irgen ber: Ming 叢 'a cluster' and 也 'also'; I take böleg irgen as 'a band of people', as in the pilot's nigen böleg irgen (§5); the force of ber 'also, even' is uncertain. Köl-Barγužin Tögüm-ün ežen: the Ming reads Tögüm as 窊 'hollow', and I keep 'lord of Tögüm' as 'master of the place Tögüm'; the Ming gives only 窊 'hollow' and 主人 'master'. The n in the genitives -(n)ü / -(n)u is Shiratori's bracket for the extra n the Han 訥 writes.

sentences.l: The girl (acc.), Qori-Tumad's noyan Qorilartai-Mergen-to, having been given there was.
sentences.i: and she had been given to Qorilartai-Mergen, noyan of the Qori-Tumad.
sentences.n: ökin-(n)i is glossed 女行, the Ming's 'to', but the ending is the accusative -i: the Ming is reading the object. ögdegsen is ög- 'give' + passive -de- + the past participle -gsen, 'the one given' (the pilot has ese ögdegsen 'not given' in §6); with ažuγ̇u 'there was' it is a pluperfect, 'had been given'. An accusative beside a passive is awkward and I follow the Ming's sense. Qorilartai-Mergen-(n)e: dative -(n)e, Ming 行 'to'. 'Given' here must mean given in marriage (compare 'not given to a man', pilot §6), but the word itself says only 'given'.

sentences.l: Qori-Tumad's land-in, Ariγ-Usun-at, Qorilartai-Mergen's Barγužin-Γoγ̇a-from born, Alan-Γoγ̇a name-having, girl: that.
sentences.i: She was born in the land of the Qori-Tumad, at Ariq-Usun, of Qorilartai-Mergen's Barqujin-Qo'a. That was the girl named Alan-Qo'a.
sentences.n: Barγužin-Γoγ̇ača carries the ablative, Ming 自 'from': 'born of' Barqujin-Qo'a. The ending is the short -ča; miqan-ača (§15) and keġeli-eče (§22, after a vowel) show the full -ača / -eče, so I cannot say what governs the short form. So Alan-Qo'a is the child of Qorilartai-Mergen and Barqujin-Qo'a, and the girl given away in the previous unit was her mother. The closing tere (Ming 那般 'so') is a bare 'that (one)': no copula, the sentence just identifies her. γažar-a and Ariγ-Usun-(n)a are dative-locatives in -a / -(n)a (Ming 行), back-vowel forms.

sentences.l: Qorilartai-Mergen, Qori-Tumad's own-in-land, sable, squirrel, game-having own-land, forbidding one another, vexing one another,
sentences.i: In the Qori-Tumad land that was his own, a land with sable, squirrel and game, Qorilartai-Mergen fell into mutual prohibition and vexation,
sentences.n: Two things to read first. -jan / -(i)jan is the reflexive-possessive 'one's own' (the family of -beġen, -deġen, -jüġen), Ming 自的行; the bracketed (i) is a linking vowel in γažar-tur(i)-jan, but in γažar(i)-jan, where the Ming's 自的(行) brackets a 行, it may be the accusative -i, 'their own land' as the thing at issue. And qorilaldužu maγ̇ulaldužu are two -žu converbs each carrying -ldu- 'one another': Ming 相禁約着 'restraining each other by prohibition', 煩惱着 'troubling each other'. I read a quarrel over the hunting, but the words say only that they hindered and vexed one another. The unit opens a long converb chain that runs on to the unit that ends 'there was'; I have broken it at each natural clause.

sentences.i: saying, “The game of Burqan-Qaldun can be hunted; it is a fine land, a good land,”

sentences.l: Burqan-Qaldun's lords, Burqan-Bosqaγsan, Sinči-Bajan, Urjaṅqai-among, having moved camp, come there was.
sentences.i: The lords of Burqan-Qaldun, Burqan-Bosqaqsan and Sinchi-Bayan, had moved their camp and come among the Uriangqai.
sentences.n: The subject is ežed, 'the lords' (ežen 'lord' + plural -d, Ming 主每), standing first in the nominative, with the two names in apposition; neither name has a case ending, so they are the ones who moved, not the ones moved to. Only Urjaṅqai-dur, Ming 裏 'among', is a place. The keġen that closes the previous unit has no marked subject; I carry Qorilartai-Mergen through the chain, but the ežed as the speakers cannot be excluded. I cannot tell whether the Ming meant 'the lords of Burqan-Qaldun' as a group already living among the Urjaṅqai; the grammar gives 'they moved their camp and came'. aisun is the 'come' verb aisu- of the pilot (aisuqu-ji §5, aisunqun §6; aisurun in §14 below). Its ending -n is uncertain: the Ming gives plain 來, without the 着 that marks a converb, so it may be a participle, 'having come', before ažuγ̇u 'was'.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [行]
to ask for, demand (here, a bride) [索]

sentences.l: Alan-Γoγ̇a (acc.), there asking, Dobun-Mergen's taken: the reason thus.
sentences.i: Dobun-Mergen asked for Alan-Qo'a there and took her; that is how it was.
sentences.n: abuγsan is ab- 'take' + the past participle -γsan, used as a noun, 'the taking'; josun is 'custom, right way, reason' (Ming 理) and teimü 'so', and together 'the reason of Dobun's taking is this', a formula that closes the account. γujužu: Ming 索着 'demanding, asking for' (here for a bride). Alan-Γoγ̇a-ji: -ji is the accusative after a vowel (Ming 行). tende 'there' is the locative of tere.

sentences.t: Alan-Γoγ̇a Dobün-Mergen-dür irežü qojar köġün töreġülbi.

morph.gloss: causative: cause to [part of 生了]

sentences.l: Alan-Γoγ̇a, Dobün-Mergen-to coming, two sons bore.
sentences.i: Alan-Qo'a came to Dobun-Mergen and bore two sons.
sentences.n: irežü is the imperfective converb of ire- 'come', 'coming'; Dobün-Mergen-dür 'to Dobun' with dative-locative -dür. The finite verb töreġülbi is not the töre- 'be born' of §8 (töregsen) but its causative töre-ġül-: 'cause to be born', so 'bore' (a woman) or 'begot'. Ming glosses both just 生. Keep the difference in view: it matters in §§17–22.

sentences.i: They were named Bügünütei and Belgünütei.
sentences.n: nereten is 'name-having' for several: the possessive -tei becomes -ten in the plural (-tan / -ten). büleġe is 'were' (Ming 有來), the past of bü- 'be'. Shiratori puts a comma after Bügünütei. The Ming gloss of Belgünütei, 人起, I cannot read.

sentences.t: Duwa-Soqor aqa in-ü dörben köġütü büleġe.

morph.gloss: his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
possessive: having, provided with (front-vowel form) [(有的)]

sentences.l: Duwa-Soqor, elder-brother his, four sons-having there was.
sentences.i: Dobun-Mergen's elder brother Duwa-Soqor had four sons.
sentences.n: in-ü is the third-person genitive 'his, her, its', placed after its noun (aqa in-ü 'elder brother his'). Here 'his' is Dobun-Mergen, so 'Duwa-Soqor, his elder brother'; the pronoun refers to the man of the last section, not to Duwa. köġütü is köġün 'son' + -tü 'having'.

sentences.t: Tedüi atala Duwa-Soqor aqa in-ü ügei boluba.

morph.gloss: his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: Thus while-being, Duwa-Soqor, elder-brother his, without became.
sentences.i: So matters stood, until Dobun-Mergen's brother Duwa-Soqor died.
sentences.n: ügei bolu-, 'to become without', is 'to die' by context (the Ming 無做了 says only 'became without'). atala is a- 'be' + -tala, 'while, until'. The two forms of 'become', bolu- (boluba here) and bol- (bolba, below), are one verb. in-ü again points to Dobun-Mergen.

sentences.t: Duwa-Soqor ügei boluγsan-(n)u qoina dörben köġüd in-ü

morph.gloss: his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: Duwa-Soqor without having-become's after, four sons his,
sentences.i: After Duwa-Soqor had died, his four sons
sentences.n: boluγsan-(n)u qoina: the past participle -γsan, then the genitive, then qoina 'after'. A genitive in front of qoina is the usual way to say 'after X-ing': 'after his having become without' = 'after he died'. The unit hangs; its subject, the four sons, takes the verb in the next. in-ü here is 'his', Duwa's.

sentences.t: Dobün-Mergen abaγa-juγ̇an uruγ-a ülü bolγan doramžilažu qaγačažu gežü neġübe.

morph.gloss: father's younger brother, paternal uncle [叔叔]
to look down on, slight [下覻]
to part from, separate from [分離]
to cast aside, abandon (Ming); possibly the 'say' verb ke- in an idiom [撇]

sentences.l: Dobün-Mergen, their-own uncle, as kin not making, looking down on, parting from, casting off, moved camp.
sentences.i: did not treat their uncle Dobun-Mergen as kin: they looked down on him, parted from him, cast him off, and moved away.
sentences.n: A converb chain: bolγan, doramžilažu, qaγačažu, gežü, four in a row before the one finite verb neġübe. Dobün-Mergen abaγa-juγ̇an is the object, 'their own uncle' (-juγ̇an reflexive-possessive; Ming 行 on it marks the object). uruγ-a ülü bolγan, 'not making [him] as kin': ülü is the 'not' for converbs and the present; ese, for the past, comes in §23. gežü is Ming 撇着 'casting aside'; it resembles the contracted forms of the 'say' verb (kēžü, §19), and I cannot tell whether it is a different verb or an idiom with 'say'; I follow the Ming.

sentences.t: Dörben oboγtan bolžu Dörben irgen tede bolba.
sentences.l: Dörben clan-having becoming, Dörben people, those, became.
sentences.i: So they became the Dörben clan, the Dörben people.
sentences.n: Dörben is simply 'four' used as a name, matching the four sons (Ming 姓名). oboγ-tan is 'clan-having' with the plural possessive -tan, as nereten in §10. tede 'those' is the subject; bolba, the past of bol-, closes.

sentences.i: After that, one day, Dobun-Mergen went up onto Toqochaq-Ündür to hunt.
sentences.n: teġün-ü is the genitive of tere 'that', the stem teġün- appearing before any case ending; teġün-ü qoina 'after that'. Toqočaγ-Ündür is a hill (Ming 地名 山名) and deġere 'on, upon' stands after it. göreġelere is a purposive converb in -re, 'in order to hunt' (Ming 捕獸), like the pilot's üžere 'in order to see', from the verb behind göreġesün 'game' (§9). The finite verb is γarba, from γar- 'go out, go up' (Ming 上去了).

sentences.l: The forest inside, an Urjaṅqai man, a three-year-old deer killing,
sentences.i: In the forest an Uriangqai man had killed a three-year-old deer,
sentences.n: hoi, Ming 林 'forest', with dotora 'inside': 'in the forest'. Urjaṅqadai is a man of the Urjaṅqai (Ming 部落名). čüġe-buγu is two words in the Ming: 三歲 'three years old' and 鹿 'deer'. alažu 'killing' is a converb waiting for its finite verb, two units on.

sentences.t: qabirγar in-ü abid in-ü širažu bükü-ji žoluγažu

words.reading: 中合必舌兒中合舌兒 qabirγar

morph.gloss: his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
abi (stem inferred from the Ming) = belly, innards [肚臟]
his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [part of 有的]

sentences.l: Its ribs, its entrails, roasting, the being one (acc.), meeting.
sentences.i: and Dobun-Mergen met him as he was roasting the ribs and the entrails.
sentences.n: bükü-ji is bü- 'be' + the participle -kü + the accusative -ji: 'the one who is' (Ming 有的); it is the man, the object of 'meeting', and širažu 'roasting' says what he was doing. The subject, Dobun-Mergen, carries over from the first unit of the section. in-ü is 'its', the deer's. qabirγar and abid, Ming 肋扇 and 肚臟 'ribs' and 'belly-innards', I take as plurals (-r and -d), though the Ming marks no plural on either; -r as a plural is odd, and I follow the Ming for the sense.

sentences.t: Dobun-Mergen ügülerün: "Nökör sirolγada" kēžüġü.

morph.gloss: converb of time: on speaking, as he spoke [part of 說]
to give roast (meat), apparently from šira- 'roast' (§12); stem uncertain [燒(肉)與的]
ending, uncertain; it has the shape of the dative-locative -da, but is read here as a request [part of 燒(肉)與的]

sentences.l: Dobun-Mergen, speaking: “Companion, roast-meat give!” said.
sentences.i: Dobun-Mergen said, “Friend, give me some roast meat.”
sentences.n: ügülerün, ügüle- 'speak' + -rün (Ming 說), opens the speech; kēžüġü 'said' (keġe-, written kē-, + -žüġü, the narrative past of ažuγ̇u) shuts it, so the verb comes after the speech. nökör is 'companion', Ming 伴當, (comrade, follower). širolγada, Ming 燒(肉)與的 'give roast [meat]': I read a request for roast meat: širolγa- looks like the 'roast' of šira- (§12), and the Ming says 'give roast (meat)'. -da has the shape of the dative-locative (na-da, §15) but I cannot make it that here, and I do not know what it is. The request sense rests on the Ming and on the answer ögsü in the next unit; this is the least certain word of the unit.

sentences.t: "Ögsü" keġežü

morph.gloss: optative: let it be given, I will give [part of 與(呵)]

sentences.l: “Let it be given,” saying,
sentences.i: “I will give it,” the man answered, and
sentences.n: ögsü is ög- 'give' + -sü, the optative: 'let it be given, I will give'. The Ming adds 呵 in brackets, its sign for 'if'; an answer to a request makes 'let it be given' far likelier than 'if I give', but I note the Ming's hint. keġežü 'saying' is the converb of the speech verb. The text names no new speaker; the man answering is the Urjaṅqai, who is the subject of the next unit.

sentences.t: aγ̇ušigitu žildu arasun in-ü abču čüġe-buγu-jin miqa gübčin-i Dobün-Mergen-(n)e ögbe.

morph.gloss: possessive: having, provided with (back-vowel form) [有的]
half the body cavity, a half-carcass (Ming) [半截腔子]
his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant) [行]

sentences.l: Lung-having half-carcass, hide, its, taking, three-year-old deer's meat whole (acc.) to Dobün-Mergen gave.
sentences.i: Taking the half-carcass with the lungs and its hide, he gave Dobun-Mergen the whole meat of the three-year-old deer.
sentences.n: A converb chain with two objects of 'taking' before it: abču 'taking' hangs on ögbe 'gave'. žildu, Ming 半截腔子 'half a body-cavity', is a half-carcass; I follow that. Who keeps what is not stated: 'taking' (abču) suggests that the Urjaṅqai kept the half-carcass with the lungs and the hide and gave Dobun the meat, gübčin (Ming 全) 'whole'; I leave the English as the Mongol has it. gübčin-i is the accusative of the thing given (-i after a consonant), Dobün-Mergen-(n)e the dative of who gets it. čüġe-buγu-jin: genitive -jin after the vowel.

sentences.t: Dobun-Mergen tere čüġe-buγu-ji ačižu aisurun žaγ̇ura

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [行]
to carry as a load, to pack [駄]
dative-locative: in, on (back-vowel form) [part of 路間]

sentences.l: Dobun-Mergen, that three-year-old deer (acc.) carrying as a load, when coming, on the road,
sentences.i: Dobun-Mergen was coming, carrying the three-year-old deer as a load, and on the road
sentences.n: aisurun, 'when coming', is a time converb in -run (like ügülerün 'on speaking'), Ming 來時. ačižu, Ming 駄着, 'carrying as a pack-load'. The accusative is -ji after a vowel (buγu-ji), -i after a consonant (gübčin-i). žaγ̇ura, žaγ̇ur 'middle' + -a, Ming 路間 'on the way'.

sentences.t: nigen jadaṅgi küġün köġün-beġen kötölžü jabuqu-ji žolγažu

morph.gloss: poor, in want (from jada- 'be lacking') [窮乏]
to lead, to draw along [牽引]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [行]

sentences.l: One poor man, his-own son leading, walking (acc.), met.
sentences.i: he met a poor man going along leading his own son.
sentences.n: The same pattern as §12: the one met stands in the accusative and a participle describes him (jabuqu-ji 'the one going'), the leading comes before. köġün-beġen is the reflexive-possessive -beġen 'his own son', the poor man's, not Dobun-Mergen's. jadaṅgi, Ming 窮乏, 'needy'; compare jada- in the next section.

sentences.t: Dobun-Mergen "jaγ̇un küġün či" keġen asaγasuγ̇asu

morph.gloss: to say; keġen 'saying', the converb that closes a quotation [麽道]
an element I cannot account for [part of 問呵]

sentences.l: Dobun-Mergen: “What man you?” saying, when asked,
sentences.i: When Dobun-Mergen asked, “What sort of man are you?”
sentences.n: No copula: jaγ̇un küġün či is 'what man you'. keġen closes the quoted words; asaγasuγ̇asu is Ming 問呵 'if / when asked', the conditional -γ̇asu with the Ming's 呵 again. The printed form has an extra -su- inside that I cannot account for.

sentences.t: tere küġün ügülerün: "Bi Maγ̇aliγ-Bajaγ̇udai jadažu jabumu.

morph.gloss: converb of time: on speaking [part of 說]

words.reading: 馬阿里黑-伯牙兀歹 Maγ̇aliγ-Bajaγ̇udai

morph.gloss: Maqaliq-Bayaqudai, a clan name (Ming 姓氏); the Ming glosses it 人名 'a personal name' in §18 [姓氏]
to be in want, to lack [窮乏]

sentences.l: That man, speaking: “I Maγ̇aliγ-Bajaγ̇udai, being in want, go about.”
sentences.i: the man answered, “I am of the Maqaliq Bayaqudai, and I go about in want.
sentences.n: jabumu: jabu- 'walk, go about' + -mu, the present tense (Ming 行有). jadažu, Ming 窮乏着, a converb on jada- 'be in want' (it also means 'be unable', §19). Maγ̇aliγ-Bajaγ̇udai is a clan name (Ming 姓氏), not a personal name. The speech runs on through three sentences to ögsü.

sentences.t: Tere göre ġesün-ü miqan-ača na-da ög.

morph.gloss: game; first half of a word the edition prints split [野物]
game; second half of the split word [的]
meat (the stem is miqan; its n shows before an ending) [肉]
I; its stem before a case ending is na- [我]
to give; the bare stem is the imperative [與]

sentences.l: That game's meat-from, to me give.
sentences.i: Give me some of the meat of that game.
sentences.n: ög, the bare stem, is the plain imperative, 'give!'. na-da shows that bi 'I' has the stem na- before a case ending (bi / na-da / min-u). Shiratori prints göreġesün-ü split across two entries (göre | ġesün-ü); the Ming glosses them 野物 and 的, 'game' and 'of', as if the break were real. miqan-ača: the stem is miqa(n), its final n showing before an ending; ablative -ača, Ming 裏 'from'.

sentences.t: Bi ene köġün-beġen čima-da ögsü" kēžüġü.

morph.gloss: you; its stem before a case ending is čima- [你]
optative: let me give, I will give [part of 與]

sentences.l: “I this son-my-own you-to give,” said.
sentences.i: And I will give you this son of mine,” he said.
sentences.n: čima- is the stem of či 'you' before a case ending, as na- is for bi. ögsü is the optative of ög- again (§13): 'I will give'. The Ming gives 與 with no 'if' this time. The man offers his son to Dobun for the meat; §16 shows what came of it. Quote closes at ögsü, then kēžüġü 'said'.

sentences.t: Dobün-Mergen tere üge-dür čüġe-buγu-jin oreġele γuja in-ü quγulžü ögčü

morph.gloss: one of a pair, a piece; form uncertain [一隻]
his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: Dobün-Mergen, that word-at, the three-year-old deer's one thigh, its, breaking off, giving,
sentences.i: At these words Dobun-Mergen broke off one thigh of the deer and gave it,
sentences.n: üge-dür, Ming 言語裏 'in the word': on that speech, in answer to it. oreġele, Ming 一隻 'one piece' (I take 'one of a pair'; the form is uncertain); γuja is the thigh, Ming 腿. quγulžü and ögčü are converbs, 'breaking off, giving': they mean 'broke off and gave'. The converb -žü has the form -čü after a consonant (ög-čü, as ab-ču above).

sentences.t: tere köġün-(n)i in-ü abčiražü ger dotora žaružu aqu büleġe.

morph.gloss: his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to bring along (ab- 'take' plus a second verb; form uncertain) [將(來)]
to employ, use as a servant [使]
participle: the one who -s [part of 住]

sentences.l: That son (acc.), his, bringing, house inside employing, staying there was.
sentences.i: and brought the poor man's son along, and lived on in the house, employing him.
sentences.n: köġün-(n)i in-ü 'that son of his', accusative (Ming 行), 'his' being the poor man's. Three verbs in a row, žaružu aqu büleġe: a converb 'employing', a participle 'staying', and 'was': a continuous 'was staying, employing him'. The Ming has 使着 'making use of' 住 'dwelling' 有來. The subject of aqu büleġe is not marked; I carry Dobun-Mergen through the chain.

sentences.t: Tein atala Dobun-Mergen ügei bolba.
sentences.l: Thus while-being, Dobun-Mergen without became.
sentences.i: So things stood, until Dobun-Mergen died.
sentences.n: tein is 'so' (Ming 那般), like tedüi in §11; atala 'while'; ügei bolba 'became without' = died, as in §11. The edition varies Dobun / Dobün in the name.

sentences.t: Dobun-Mergen-i ügei boluγsa- n-u qoina

morph.gloss: past participle, first part: the edition breaks it across two entries [part of 做了]
past participle, last letter n carried over from the previous entry [part of 的]

sentences.l: Dobun-Mergen (acc.) without having-become's after,
sentences.i: After Dobun-Mergen's death,
sentences.n: Dobun-Mergen-i is accusative (Ming 行), though English wants a plain subject: I take the accusative as marking the subject of the participle clause, as the Ming's 行 suggests; it is awkward, and §11 (Duwa-Soqor ügei boluγsan-(n)u qoina) has a plain subject instead. The edition splits the participle across two entries (boluγsa- | n-u, Ming 做了 | 的): one word boluγsan-u, as in §11, 'of having become [without]', then qoina 'after'.

sentences.t: Alan-Γoγ̇a ere ügeiġüi böġed γurban köġüd töreġülbi.

morph.gloss: a form of ügei 'without'; the added -ġüi is the negative ending, redundant here; uncertain [無]
converb ending: 'being so, even so'; uncertain [part of 便]
causative: cause to [part of 生了]

sentences.l: Alan-Γoγ̇a, husband without, even so three sons bore.
sentences.i: Alan-Qo'a, though she had no husband, bore three sons.
sentences.n: ere ügeiġüi, 'husband without'. The form ügeiġüi is odd: ügei 'without' with a negative ending -ġüi added (Han 兀該爲, Ming gloss 無); the next section writes ügelġüi, perhaps a misprint of ügeiġüi. böġed, Ming 便 'at once, even so': I take it as a converb of bü- 'be' (the stem böġe- of the pilot's böġesü), 'being so'. The Ming 便 says only 'then, thereupon'; 'though' is the sense the context gives (no husband, yet sons), not something the word says. The sentence turns on it: no husband, and still sons. töreġülbi is the causative again: 'bore'.

sentences.t: Buγu-Qatagi, Buqatu-Salži, Bodončar-Muṅqaγ nereten büleġe.

words.reading: 孛端察舌兒-蒙中合黑 Bodončar-Muṅqaγ

morph.gloss: Bodonchar-Munqaq, a son's name; Muṅqaγ is an epithet [(兒)名]

sentences.l: Buγu-Qatagi, Buqatu-Salži, Bodončar-Muṅqaγ, name-having they were.
sentences.i: Their names were Buqu-Qatagi, Buqatu-Salji and Bodonchar-Munqaq.
sentences.n: nereten as in §10, 'name-having', plural. Bodončar-Muṅqaγ is the last listed; Muṅqaγ is an epithet, 'foolish, simple' (Ming 愚 in §23, where it is a plain word). Shiratori has a comma after Qatagi and after Salži, none after Muṅqaγ.

sentences.t: Urida Dobun-Mergen-eče töregsen Belgünütei, Bügünütei qojar köġüd in-ü eke-jüġen Alan-Γoγ̇a-jin ečine ügüleldürün:

words.reading: 朶奔-篾舌兒格捏扯 Dobun-Mergen-eče

morph.gloss: Belgünütei; the Ming gloss cannot be read [人起]
his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
behind, at the back of, out of sight [背處]
converb of time: while speaking [part of 共說]

sentences.l: Formerly Dobun-Mergen-from born Belgünütei, Bügünütei two sons, their, mother-their-own Alan-Γoγ̇a's behind, speaking together:
sentences.i: The two sons born earlier to Dobun-Mergen, Belgünütei and Bügünütei, were talking together behind their mother Alan-Qo'a's back:
sentences.n: Take the first half as a name-list with a participle: Dobun-Mergen-eče töregsen 'born of Dobun-Mergen' (ablative -eče, 'from'), then the two sons. in-ü after köġüd can point back to Dobun-Mergen ('his two sons') or mean 'their'; with eke-jüġen 'their own mother' beside it the possession is said twice either way, and I leave in-ü out of the English. ečine, Ming 背處, 'behind, at the back': out of her hearing. ügüleldürün is ügüle- + reciprocal -ldu- + -rün, 'speaking among themselves'. The quotation follows.

sentences.t: "Ene eke bidan-u aqa deġü ujaγaja küġün ügei,

morph.gloss: we, inclusive of the person addressed; bidan- is its stem before a case ending [咱]
near kin of the same branch; form unclear [房親]

sentences.l: “This mother, of us, elder-brother, younger-brother, kinsman, man, without,
sentences.i: “This mother of ours has none of our elder or younger brothers, no kinsman, no man,
sentences.n: No verb: ügei 'without' stands alone as the predicate. bidan-u is 'of us' (bida, the inclusive 'we', stem bidan-), and I read it as governing aqa deġü ujaγaja küġün, 'our elder brothers, younger brothers, kin, men'. Whether the speakers mean their father's side or the mother's own kin the words do not say; I give the first because the next lines ask who the father can be. ujaγaja, Ming 房親 'near kin of the same branch', is unclear in form. The comma after ügei is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: ere ügelġüi böġetele ede γurban köġüd töreġülbi.

morph.gloss: without; ügelġüi is a spelling variant, perhaps a misprint, of ügeiġüi (§17) [無]
causative: cause to [part of 生了]

sentences.l: Husband without although, these three sons bore.
sentences.i: and though she has no husband, she has borne these three sons.
sentences.n: ere ügelġüi 'husband without'; böġetele is bü- 'be' (böġe-) + the converb -tele, Ming 旣 'already, since': 'she being so — husbandless — yet ...'; 'though' is the sense the context gives. ede is the plural of ene 'this'. töreġülbi, causative, 'bore'. The speech is still going.

sentences.t: ger dotora γaγča Maγ̇aliγ-Bajaγ̇udai küġün bijü.

words.reading: 馬阿里黑-伯牙兀歹 Maγ̇aliγ-Bajaγ̇udai

morph.gloss: Maqaliq-Bayaqudai, the clan name of §15, here glossed 人名 [(人名)]

sentences.l: House inside, alone, Maγ̇aliγ-Bajaγ̇udai man is.
sentences.i: In the house there is only the Maqaliq-Bayaqudai man.
sentences.n: γaγča 'alone, only' makes the sentence 'only the Maqaliq-Bayaqudai man is in the house': presumably the poor man's son whom Dobun took in (§16). bijü, Ming 有, 'is, there is': the present of bü- 'be', as in the pilot (§6). The Ming glosses Maγ̇aliγ-Bajaγ̇udai 人名 here, 姓氏 'clan name' in §15; it is the same name.

sentences.t: ede γurban köġüd teġün-ü-ġei bi-že"

morph.gloss: that; teġün- is its stem before a case ending [他]
belonging to, 'his own' [part of 他的]
to be; the stem shows as bi- before -že [有]
particle of assertion: indeed, surely [part of 有]

sentences.l: These three sons his-own are indeed.”
sentences.i: These three sons must be his.”
sentences.n: teġün-ü-ġei is teġün-ü 'of that one' + -ġei, which I take as 'belonging to' from its shape (the Ming 他的 glosses only teġün-ü): 'his own, his'. bi-že is bi- 'be' + the assertive particle -že, 'it surely is' (Ming 有; the same -že is glossed 也者 in bijü-že, §21). The quotation ends. Why they think so is the reason in the line before: in the house there is only that man.

sentences.t: keġen eke-jüġen ečine keleldüküi-ji eke an-u Alan-Γoγ̇a uqažu

morph.gloss: to say; keġen 'saying', the converb that closes a quotation [麽道]
behind, at the back of [背處]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [行]
their (the back-vowel companion of in-ü) [他的]

sentences.l: Saying, mother-their-own behind (their) speaking together (acc.), their mother Alan-Γoγ̇a finding out,
sentences.i: Such was their talk, behind their mother's back, and their mother Alan-Qo'a found out,
sentences.n: keġen closes the quotation. keleldüküi-ji is kele- 'speak' + reciprocal -ldü- + the participle -küi + accusative -ji: 'their talking together', the thing she found out (uqažu, Ming 覺着, 'perceiving'). The unit ends on a converb, uqažu, so its main verb is in the next section: the chain jumps the section break.

sentences.t: qabur nigen üdür küṅsilemel qonin činažu

morph.gloss: Ming 臘, 'winter-cured, preserved'; the Mongol word is uncertain [臘]

sentences.l: Spring, one day, winter-cured(?) sheep boiling,
sentences.i: One spring day she boiled a sheep, winter-cured (?),
sentences.n: qabur is 'spring' (Ming 春). küṅsilemel is glossed 臘 — the winter sacrifice, and meat cured in winter; 'winter-cured' is my guess at what the glossator meant. The Mongol word I cannot analyse, so the sense of 'a küṅsilemel sheep' is uncertain. činažu 'boiling', Ming 煮着, the converb which waits for the verb 'gave'. The subject, Alan-Qo'a, carries over from §18.

sentences.t: Belgünütei, Bügünütei, Buγu-Qatagi, Buqatu-Salži, Bodončar-Muṅqaγ ede tabun köġüd(i)-jen žergelen saγ̇ulžu

words.reading: 孛端察舌兒-蒙中合黑 Bodončar-Muṅqaγ

morph.gloss: her own, with accusative i [(自的)行]
adverbial, 'in a row'; uncertain [part of 列]

sentences.l: Belgünütei, Bügünütei, Buγu-Qatagi, Buqatu-Salži, Bodončar-Muṅqaγ, these five sons-her-own (acc.) in a row seating,
sentences.i: and had her five sons, Belgünütei, Bügünütei, Buqu-Qatagi, Buqatu-Salji and Bodonchar-Munqaq, sit in a row,
sentences.n: A name-list in apposition to ede tabun köġüd(i)-jen. The bracketed (i) in köġüd(i)-jen is, I take it, the accusative -i (the Ming's 行 marks the object), which Shiratori brackets; -jen is the reflexive-possessive 'her own'. žergelen, Ming 列, 'in a row' (žerge 'row'); saγ̇ulžu is saγ̇ul-, the causative of saγu- 'sit', 'making sit'.

sentences.t: nižiġed müsüd quγuludqun keġežü ögbe.

morph.gloss: one each, one apiece; form uncertain [每一隻]

words.reading: 中忽中忽魯惕中渾 quγuludqun

morph.gloss: imperative(-optative): 'do break'; the inner -ud- is unexplained and the Ming adds 您 'you' [您]

sentences.l: One-each arrow-shafts “break!” saying, gave.
sentences.i: and gave each of them one arrow-shaft, saying, “Break it.”
sentences.n: quγuludqun, Ming 折折您: quγul- 'break' plus an ending of command, in which I see -qun (compare baiγ̇ulqun below) and an unexplained -ud-; the Ming 您 'you' (honorific) hints at a plural address, but quγugdaqun and bolqun in §22 have the same -qun without any 您. nižiġed, Ming 每一隻 'one apiece'. müsü 'arrow-shaft' with the plural -d. keġežü 'saying' and ögbe 'gave' form a pair: 'saying … gave'.

sentences.t: Nižiġed-i jaγ̇u baiγ̇ulqun quγučižu oγ̇orba.

morph.gloss: to go off, depart (stem unknown; Ming 去了 may also mean 'done') [去]

sentences.l: Single (acc.) how(?) let-be-set, each breaking, went off.
sentences.i: Each of them broke his single arrow and went off.
sentences.n: The middle of this unit is where I am unsure. Nižiġed-i jaγ̇u baiγ̇ulqun: Ming 一隻行 怎 敎停住, 'single (acc.), how, make stop'. jaγ̇u is 'what, how'; baiγ̇ul- is the causative of bai- 'stand, stay', 'make stand, set down'. I cannot construe the sequence with confidence and the idiomatic line gives only what is plain from the whole: each broke his single arrow (quγučižu, Ming 各折折着 'each breaking'), and they went off (oγ̇orba, Ming 去了 'gone'; I do not know the stem, and 去了 may be a completive, 'done', rather than 'went away').

sentences.t: Basa tabun müsüd qamtu čuγlažu quγuludqun kēžü ögbe.

words.reading: 中忽中忽魯惕中渾 quγuludqun

morph.gloss: imperative(-optative): 'do break'; the inner -ud- is unexplained and the Ming adds 您 'you' [您]

sentences.l: Again five arrow-shafts together bundling, “break!” saying, gave.
sentences.i: Again she bundled five shafts together and said, “Break them,” and gave them over.
sentences.n: Basa 'again' marks the second trial. qamtu 'together' (Ming 一同); čuγla- 'bundle', Ming 束着. The second kēžü is keġe- + -žü 'saying', the contracted form of keġežü. The command is the same quγuludqun as in the first trial.

sentences.t: Tabuγ̇ula tabun čuγtai müsüd küġüleldün barižu bitüġülžü quγuluu jadaba.

morph.gloss: each man, one by one; form uncertain [每人]
to take in turn (Ming 輪着); form uncertain [輪]
converb ending ('-ing'); printed quγuluu, but the Han 侖 reads lun, so quγulun [part of 折折]
to be unable, to lack the strength [不能]

sentences.l: All five, five bundled arrow-shafts, each-man taking, in turn, breaking, could not.
sentences.i: Each of the five took the bundle of five shafts in turn and tried to break it, and could not.
sentences.n: tabun-γ̇ula 'all five' (the suffix -γ̇ula = 'the whole lot'; compare dörbeġule, §23). čuγtai is čuγ 'bundle' + -tai 'having': 'bundled'. küġüleldün, Ming 每人 'each man', and bitüġülžü, Ming 輪着 'in turn', are both of uncertain form. quγuluu is probably a misprint: the Han 中忽中忽侖 ends in 侖 (lun), so the word is quγulun, 'breaking'. jadaba is jada- 'be unable' (Ming 不能了) + -ba; the same verb meant 'be in want' in §15.

sentences.t: Tende Alan-Γoγ̇a eke in-ü ügülebi.

morph.gloss: his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: There, Alan-Γoγ̇a, mother their, said.
sentences.i: Then their mother Alan-Qo'a spoke.
sentences.n: tende 'there, then' is the locative of tere. in-ü 'their' after eke, as in §18. ügülebi: ügüle- + -bi, the past tense. The speech follows.

sentences.t: "Ta Belgünütei, Bügünütei qojar köġüd min-u nama-ji ede γurban köġüd-i töreġülbi.

morph.gloss: I; min- is its genitive stem [我]
genitive: of (here set after its noun: my) [的]
I; nama- is its stem before the accusative [我]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [行]
causative: cause to [part of 生了]

sentences.l: “You Belgünütei, Bügünütei, two sons my: me (acc.), these three sons (acc.) caused-to-be-born.
sentences.i: “You two, Belgünütei and Bügünütei, are my sons; and it was to me that these three sons were born.
sentences.n: Hard sentence: ta … qojar köġüd min-u 'you, Belgünütei, Bügünütei, two sons of mine' (min-u set after its noun, 'my'). Then nama-ji, 'me' in the accusative (the stem nama- before the ending), and ede γurban köġüd-i 'these three sons' (accusative), with the causative töreġülbi 'caused to be born' last. Two accusatives under a causative would read 'someone caused me to bear these three sons'; the agent is not named here. The Ming reads nama-ji as 我行 'to me', and I translate 'were born to me', which keeps that sense without naming an agent. This is the least sure sentence of the unit. ta is the plural, polite 'you'.

sentences.t: Ken-ü jaγ̇un-u köġüd bijü, keġen sereldün keleldümüi.

morph.gloss: to say; keġen 'saying', the converb that closes a quotation [麽道]
reciprocal: one another [part of 疑的]

sentences.l: ‘Whose, what's sons are they?’ saying, suspecting each other, you speak together.
sentences.i: You are asking each other whose sons they are, and voicing your doubts.
sentences.n: ken-ü jaγ̇un-u, 'whose, of what'; the second is a doubled question. keġen closes the thought; sereldün is sere- 'be wary, suspect' + reciprocal -ldü- + converb -n (Ming 疑的); keleldümüi is kele- + -ldü- + the present -müi (Ming 共說有), 'you talk together'.

sentences.t: Sereküi ber tan-u žöb.

morph.gloss: you (plural, polite); tan- is its stem before a case ending [您]

sentences.l: Suspecting too your right.
sentences.i: Your suspicion, too, is right.
sentences.n: sereküi is the participle of sere-; ber 'even, also'; tan-u 'your' (ta, plural 'you', stem tan-) and žöb, Ming 是, 'right, correct'. No copula: 'your suspecting also right'.

sentences.t: Sünid büri čegen šira küġün ger-ün erüge dotoγa-jin gegeġer orožu

morph.gloss: smoke-hole, roof-window of the tent [天窗]
the door-lintel, the upper edge of the doorway (Ming); uncertain [門額]
instrumental or locative: by, in; uncertain [裏]

sentences.l: Nights each bright yellow man, the tent's smoke-hole's door-lintel's light-in entering,
sentences.i: Every night a bright yellow man came in by the light at the smoke-hole,
sentences.n: Sünid büri, 'nights each' (Ming 夜 每): every night. A string of genitives ends in the light: ger-ün erüge dotoγa-jin gegeġer, Ming 房的天窗門額的明裏, 'in the light of the lintel of the smoke-hole of the tent'. dotoγa (Ming 門額, the door-lintel; it may be related to dotora 'inside', but I follow the Ming) is uncertain; gegeġer, with its -r, may be 'in, by the light'. I keep the Ming's order and have simplified it in the English. The unit is a converb and waits.

sentences.t: keġeli min-u biližü gegeġen in-ü keġeli-dür min-u siṅgekü büleġe.

morph.gloss: I; min- is its genitive stem [我]
his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
I; min- is its genitive stem [我]

sentences.l: Belly my stroking, bright his belly-in my penetrating there was.
sentences.i: and stroked my belly, and his brightness was soaking into my belly.
sentences.n: keġeli min-u, 'belly my' (the possessive after its noun), bili- … biližü, Ming 摩着, 'stroking'. gegeġen in-ü: 'bright(ness) his'. siṅgekü büleġe: the participle siṅge- 'soak in, penetrate' + 'was', a continuous past, 'was soaking in'. keġeli-dür: dative-locative -dür, 'into'.

sentences.t: Γarurun naran sara-jin kili-jer šira noγai metü sičabalžažu γarqu büleġe.

morph.gloss: ray, beam (inferred from the Ming 透入光裏); uncertain [透入光]
instrumental or locative (compare -ber in Teġü-ber; the choice between -jer and -ber is not explained); uncertain [裏]
participle: the one who -s [part of 出]

sentences.l: Going out when, sun moon's penetrating-light-in, yellow dog like, crawling, going out there was.
sentences.i: And when he went out, he was crawling out by the shining rays of the sun and the moon, like a yellow dog.
sentences.n: Γarurun, γar- 'go out' + the time converb: 'on going out' (Ming 出時). kili-jer, Ming 透入光裏 'in the penetrating light': kili I take as 'ray, beam' from the Ming, with -jer 'in, by' (an instrumental or locative, compare -ber in Teġü-ber, §21 below, though why -jer here and -ber there I cannot say; the Ming glosses it 裏 'in'); both uncertain. šira noγai metü, 'yellow dog like': metü is a postposition 'like, as' (Ming 般). sičabalžažu, Ming 爬着, 'crawling'. γarqu büleġe: 'was going out'.

sentences.t: Deleme jakin ügüled ta.

morph.gloss: verb ending that goes with a plural subject (here ta 'you'); uncertain [part of 說]

sentences.l: Rashly how speaking you.
sentences.i: Why do you speak so rashly?
sentences.n: deleme, Ming 造次, 'rashly, hastily'; jakin 'how, why'. ügüled ta, Ming 說 … 塔, 'speak you': -d I take as a verb ending that goes with a plural subject (compare uqad-že, below), but I am not sure. ta is the plural, polite 'you'.

sentences.t: Teġü-ber uqaγ̇asu temdeg in-ü teṅgiri-jin köġüd bijü-že.

morph.gloss: that; teġü- is its stem before a case ending [那般]
sign, mark; the Ming reads it 'plain, clear' [明白]
his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
Heaven, the sky as a power [天]

sentences.l: By that, if understanding, sign (clear) his, of Heaven sons they are indeed.
sentences.i: By this, if you understand it, the sign is plain: they are the sons of Heaven.
sentences.n: teġü-ber, Ming 爲那般 'for that reason': the instrumental -ber on the stem teġü- of tere. uqaγ̇asu, 'if you understand'. temdeg, Ming 明白 'plain', but the Mongol word is 'sign'; in-ü after it I read as 'its' (the sign of this). teṅgeri-jin köġüd 'of Heaven sons': possessor before noun. bijü-že, 'they are indeed': the particle -že, Ming 也者.

sentences.t: Qara teriġü,ü küġün-dür qanilγan jakin ügüled ta.

morph.gloss: possessive: having; printed teriġü,ü, but the Han reads teriġütü [(有的)]
to liken, compare; form unclear [比着]
verb ending that goes with a plural subject (here ta 'you'); uncertain [part of 說]

sentences.l: Black head-having man-to comparing how speaking you.
sentences.i: Why do you speak, comparing them to an ordinary black-headed man?
sentences.n: qara teriġü,ü: 'black head-having', probably a way to say 'ordinary people' (the contrast with qād and qaračus in the next unit suggests it); the Ming gives only 'black head-having man'. The printed teriġü,ü does not match the Han, which reads teriġütü (禿 tu); the Han is the safer guide. küġün-dür, dative-locative 'to'. qanilγan, Ming 比着 'comparing': the stem is unclear.

sentences.t: Qamuγ-un qād boluγ̇asu qaračus tende uqad-že" keġebe.

morph.gloss: sovereign, emperor; qād is the plural, contracted [帝王(每)]
verb ending that goes with a plural subject (here the commoners); uncertain [part of 省]
particle of assertion: indeed [part of 省]

sentences.l: All-of sovereigns if they become, commoners there will understand,” said.
sentences.i: When they become the sovereigns of all, then the common people will understand,” she said.
sentences.n: Qamuγ-un qād boluγ̇asu: 'of-all sovereigns, if they become'. qād is the contracted plural of qaγan (Ming 帝王(每)); qaračus, the plural of qarača (Ming 下民). uqad-že, Ming 省, 'let them understand, they will know': the -d ending and the particle -že are uncertain in force. keġebe, 'said', closes the speech.

sentences.t: Basa Alan-Γoγ̇a tabun köġüd-teġen süjüġer üge ügülerün;

morph.gloss: converb of time: speaking [part of 說]

sentences.l: Again, Alan-Γoγ̇a, five sons-her-own instruction word, speaking:
sentences.i: Again Alan-Qo'a spoke her teaching to her five sons:
sentences.n: köġüd-teġen is köġün + plural -d + reflexive-possessive -teġen, 'to her own sons' (Ming 行). süjüġer, Ming 敎訓, 'teaching, admonition'; its form is not clear to me. ügülerün opens the speech as before; here Shiratori ends the unit with a semicolon, not a colon.

sentences.t: "Ta tabun köġüd min-u γaγča keġeli-eče törebe.

morph.gloss: I; min- is its genitive stem [我]

sentences.l: “You five sons my single belly-from were born.
sentences.i: “You five sons were born of my one belly.
sentences.n: töre-be: here the plain intransitive 'was born', not the causative of §§17–20. keġeli-eče, ablative -eče, Ming 處 'from'. γaγča 'single, alone': she insists on one belly, one mother.

sentences.t: Ta tuγarun tabun müsüd metü, γaγča γaγča boluγ̇asu

morph.gloss: just now, a moment ago [恰纔]

sentences.l: You just-now five arrows like, single single if you become,
sentences.i: If you each become alone, like the five arrows just now,
sentences.n: tuγarun, Ming 恰纔, 'just now' (the arrows broken). metü 'like'. γaγča γaγča 'single, single' doubled for 'each one alone'; boluγ̇asu 'if you become'. Shiratori's comma after metü breaks the sentence between 'like' and the condition, which I have kept.

sentences.t: tere nižiġed müsüd metü, ken-e ber kilbar-a quγugdaqun ta.

morph.gloss: one each, a single one [一隻]
dative-locative used as an adverb: easily [行]

words.reading: 中忽中忽(黑)荅中渾 quγugdaqun

sentences.l: That single arrow like, by anyone even easily may be broken, you.
sentences.i: then, like a single arrow, you may be broken easily by anyone.
sentences.n: quγugdaqun is quγul- + the passive -γda- (the l is lost in the printed form) + -qun, 'you may be broken' (Ming 被折折 'be broken'). ken-e ber, Ming 任誰也, 'even by anyone, by anyone at all'. kilbar-a, Ming 容易行, 'easily': an adjective with the dative-locative -a used as an adverb. ta closes, 'you'.

sentences.t: Tere čuγtai müsüd metü qamtu nigen ejeten boluγ̇asu

morph.gloss: 'of one counsel', united (Ming 商量有的); form uncertain [商量有(的每)]

sentences.l: That bundled arrow-shafts like, together, one counsel-having if you become,
sentences.i: But if you become one in counsel, together, like those bundled arrows,
sentences.n: ejeten, Ming 商量有(的每), 'having counsel'. I read it as 'of one counsel' (agreed, united) from the Ming; the form is unclear. nigen ejeten, 'one-counsel-having'. qamtu 'together' (Ming 一同). The conditional is boluγ̇asu again. čuγtai 'bundled', as in §19.

sentences.t: ken-e-ber kilbar-a jakin bolqun ta" keġebi.

morph.gloss: dative-locative used as an adverb: easily [行]
to become; here 'be undone' (Ming 壞 'spoil') [壞]

sentences.l: By anyone even easily how undone you,” said.
sentences.i: how could anyone easily break you?” she said.
sentences.n: The answer is a question: jakin bolqun ta, 'how would you be undone?' bolqun, Ming 壞 'spoil': I take it as 'be undone, be broken', with the same ending -qun as quγugdaqun. ken-e-ber is the same as ken-e ber before, 'by anyone at all'. keġebi: keġe- + -bi, the past.

sentences.t: Atala Alan-Γoγ̇a eke an-u ügei bolbi.
sentences.l: While remaining, Alan-Γoγ̇a mother their without became.
sentences.i: Some time passed, and their mother Alan-Qo'a died.
sentences.n: atala 'while, until' (a- + -tala), here 'as time went on'; ügei bolbi 'became without' = died, as before. an-u 'their' after its noun, the back-vowel companion of in-ü; the Ming glosses both 他的, and in-ü also stands where 'their' is meant (§20), so I cannot say the two differ in number.

sentences.t: eke-jüġen Alan-Γoγ̇a-ji ügei boluγsan-u qoina aqa-nar deġü-ner tabuγ̇ula adusun ideġe-ben qubijaldurun

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [行]

words.reading: 中忽必牙(勒)都︀舌侖 qubijaldurun

morph.gloss: reciprocal: one another [part of 分時]

sentences.l: Mother-their-own Alan-Γoγ̇a (acc.) without having-become's after, elder-brothers, younger-brothers, all five, livestock, food-their-own, when dividing,
sentences.i: After their mother Alan-Qo'a had died, the five brothers, when they divided the herds and their food,
sentences.n: The participle clause again: Alan-Γoγ̇a-ji … ügei boluγsan-u qoina, 'after her having become without' with an accusative on the subject, as in §17. aqa-nar and deġü-ner are the plural of 'elder brother' and 'younger brother'; the plural is -nar after a back vowel and -ner after a front one. tabuγ̇ula 'all five' (-γ̇ula, 'the whole'). qubijaldurun, qubija- 'divide' + reciprocal -ldu- + -run, Ming 分時, 'when sharing out'. eke-jüġen and ideġe-ben are reflexive-possessives.

sentences.t: Belgünütei, Bügünütei Buγu-Qatagi, Buqatu-Salži, dörbeġule abulčaba.
sentences.l: Belgünütei, Bügünütei, Buγu-Qatagi, Buqatu-Salži, all four took among themselves.
sentences.i: the four of them, Belgünütei, Bügünütei, Buqu-Qatagi and Buqatu-Salji, took it among themselves.
sentences.n: dörbeġule is dörben 'four' + -ġule, 'all four together'. abulčaba is ab- 'take' + -ulča-, Ming 相要了, 'took among themselves, took for themselves jointly'. The four are the first four listed; the fifth, Bodonchar, is left out.

sentences.t: Bodončar muṅqaγ budaγ̇u bijü, keġen

morph.gloss: to say; keġen 'saying', the converb that closes a quotation [麽道]

sentences.l: Bodončar, simple, weak he is, saying,
sentences.i: Saying, “Bodonchar is a simpleton, and weak,”
sentences.n: muṅqaγ, Ming 愚, 'foolish, simple'; here it is a plain adjective, though it also appears in his name. budaγ̇u, Ming 弱, 'weak, feeble'. bijü 'is'. keġen closes the thought, the brothers' reason.

sentences.t: uruγ-a ülü toγ̇an qubi ese ögbe.

morph.gloss: not (negates the past): did not, has not yet [不曾]

sentences.l: Kin-as not counting, share not gave.
sentences.i: they did not count him as kin, and gave him no share.
sentences.n: Two negatives in one line, and they are different: ülü (uruγ-a ülü toγ̇an, 'not counting as kin', with the converb) and ese (qubi ese ögbe, 'share did not give', with the past). Mongol keeps ülü for the present and converbs and ese for the past. toγ̇an, from toγ̇a- 'count' (Ming 數). uruγ-a is the dative-like 'as kin' of §11.
